cfallin opened PR #14776 from cfallin:gdbstub-forward-interrupts to bytecodealliance:main:

The gdbstub component acknowledged a client's interrupt request (Ctrl-C) without asking the debuggee to stop, so interrupting a running program had no effect until its next debug event. Call debuggee.interrupt() and report the resulting interrupted event as the stop.

This PR also adds a protocol-level test, using a minimal GDB remote protocol client, that interrupts a long-running loop. (This little test stub is also useful for later PRs I plan to send.)

:thumbs_up: alexcrichton submitted PR review:

I won't really pretend to understand the test, but seems reasonable otherwise.

One thing I'll point out though, which is preexisting, is that free_port is inherently a racy function. Eventually we'll probably see flakes due to that. If you (or perhaps an LLM) have a chance, it'd be best to spawn wasmtime bound to port 0, have Wasmtime print out where it's listening, read that from the test, and then use that.
